description: Sayadieh is a classic Middle Eastern fish and rice dish, celebrated for its deeply flavorful rice infused with fish stock and aromatic spices. Layers of tender white fish and perfectly caramelized onions create a harmonious balance of sweet and savory notes, making it a truly comforting and elegant meal. This traditional recipe brings the authentic taste of the Mediterranean coast right to your table, perfect for family gatherings or a special weeknight dinner.

ingredients.notes: cod, snapper, or halibut, skinless and boneless

instructions.title: Caramelize the Onions
instructions.text: Heat 1/4 cup of olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add the thinly sliced yellow onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until they are deeply caramelized, dark brown, and very sweet. Be patient, as this step is crucial for flavor and color. Remove about half of the caramelized onions and set aside for garnish.

instructions.title: Prepare and Fry the Fish
instructions.text: While onions are caramelizing, pat the fish fillets dry and season generously with salt and black pepper. Dredge each fillet lightly in all-purpose flour, shaking off any excess. Heat a few tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the fish fillets for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside on a plate.

instructions.title: Infuse the Fish Stock with Spices
instructions.text: In the pot with the remaining caramelized onions, add the cumin powder, coriander powder, allspice, and turmeric powder. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in the fish stock, bring it to a gentle simmer, and let it cook for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Cook the Sayadieh Rice
instructions.text: Add the rinsed basmati rice to the spiced fish stock and caramelized onions in the pot. Stir gently to combine. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.

instructions.title: Assemble the Dish
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes. Gently flake the cooked fish into large pieces. Fluff the rice with a fork, then carefully fold in most of the flaked fish. You can layer it or mix it gently, ensuring not to break the fish into very small pieces.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the Sayadieh fish rice to a large serving platter. Garnish generously with the reserved caramelized onions, toasted pine nuts, and freshly chopped parsley. Serve immediately, perhaps with a side of lemon wedges or a simple cucumber and tomato salad.

tips: Achieving truly dark, deeply caramelized onions is key to Sayadieh's signature color and sweet flavor. Cook them slowly over medium-low heat for at least 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are a rich, dark brown, almost black, but not burnt.

For the most authentic flavor, use a homemade fish stock made from fish heads and bones. If using store-bought, enhance it by simmering with a piece of onion, a bay leaf, and a few peppercorns before adding to the rice.

Do not overmix the rice once it is added to the pot. Let it simmer gently and absorb the liquid. Fluff with a fork only after it has rested for 5-10 minutes off the heat, ensuring separate, fluffy grains.
